subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Gearboxes in Robots: Harmonic and Cycloidal
description: A short lesson to help you apply Gearboxes in Robots: Harmonic and Cycloidal.

hook.text: Robot motors spin fast but with little torque. Gearboxes slow them down and multiply the force at each joint.

buildup.text: Harmonic drives use a flexible cup to achieve 100:1 ratios in a disc thinner than a pancake. Zero backlash.

discovery.text: Cycloidal drives use a wobbling disc among pins. They handle shock loads that would strip harmonic drives.

twist.text: The gearbox often costs more than the motor. In a six-axis robot, gearboxes can be 40% of the total price.

climax.text: Choosing between harmonic and cycloidal defines the robot's personality — delicate precision or rugged toughness.

punchline.text: The gearbox is the robot's skeleton. It sets the limits on everything.

quiz.question: Why can gearboxes account for 40% of a robot's total cost?
options: They use exotic materials not found in other mechanical components
They require extreme precision — zero backlash and high ratios in compact form
Each gearbox must be custom-designed for every individual robot model
